data.name: Wooden Floor 2 - Resurrection
data.detailed_description:
"Wooden Floor 2 - Resurrection" is a first person horror/mystery adventure game. Just like the prequel this game is pretty much an one man project by me (Pheenix93).

The game is telling the story of Andrew Winter, an alcoholic living in a small cabin near the woods. He keeps having nightmares about an abandoned place that seems familiar to him. You have to reveal the dark secrets that are hiding in the abandoned mansion on top of the hill in Blackdust Field.
Are you able to find out the truth hiding in the deepest insides of the house?

"Wooden Floor 2 - Resurrection" is the sequel to Wooden Floor, telling the other side of the story and completing the puzzle.

Features of Wooden Floor 2:
  • Multiple endings!
  • Different playthroughs as the game changes upon choices you make, your behaviour and at certain points randomly
  • More interaction with the world
  • Secret riddles in game that may open up new possibilities for you (if you are able to reveal them)
  • Improved story telling in comparison to Wooden Floor
  • Different locations
  • Useable items
  • Big improvements to graphics and gameplay!

Besides all this there is still potential to add more content to the game once i feel like its about time. So there may be more to come...

reviews.review:
Developed and published by pheenix93, Wooden Floor 2: Resurrection is an indie first-person horror adventure that builds upon the ideas introduced in the original game while delivering a more refined and story-focused experience. Rather than relying solely on cheap scares, the game places players in the role of Andrew Winter, a troubled man plagued by disturbing dreams that repeatedly draw him toward the mysterious Blackdust Field mansion. As reality and nightmare begin to merge, the journey becomes one of uncovering forgotten memories, supernatural secrets, and the truth hidden within the walls of an abandoned estate. The narrative embraces psychological horror, inviting players to slowly unravel its mysteries through observation, exploration, and environmental storytelling.

The game's greatest strength lies in the oppressive atmosphere it creates from beginning to end. Every hallway, room, and forgotten corner of the mansion contributes to a constant sense of unease, making exploration feel tense even during moments when nothing immediately threatens the player. Clever use of lighting, eerie ambient audio, and unsettling environmental details work together to establish an immersive horror setting that encourages careful investigation instead of reckless movement. The mansion itself feels like a living puzzle, rewarding players who pay attention to subtle clues and hidden objects while maintaining an air of uncertainty that keeps the experience engaging.

Compared to its predecessor, Wooden Floor 2 introduces several improvements designed to make exploration more meaningful. Multiple endings provide genuine replay value, encouraging players to revisit the game and discover how different choices and actions influence the overall outcome. Hidden riddles, interactive objects, additional locations, and randomized events help ensure that no two playthroughs unfold exactly the same way. Rather than guiding players along a completely linear path, the game offers opportunities to experiment, revisit areas, and uncover secrets that may easily be missed during an initial playthrough. This approach strengthens the game's emphasis on mystery and discovery while rewarding curiosity with additional story elements.

The visual presentation represents a noticeable step forward for the series, featuring more detailed environments and improved lighting effects that effectively reinforce the unsettling tone. Although the production values remain modest compared to larger horror releases, the art direction successfully creates believable locations filled with personality and decay. The sound design is equally important, relying on unsettling ambient noises, distant echoes, and carefully timed silence to heighten tension throughout the adventure. The slower pacing complements these elements well, allowing players to absorb the atmosphere instead of rushing from one scripted event to another.

Despite its strengths, the game does have several limitations that reflect its independent development. Character movement and interaction can occasionally feel stiff, while some puzzles require close attention to environmental details that may leave players uncertain about how to progress. The intentionally cryptic storytelling also demands patience, as important plot details are rarely presented directly and instead must be assembled piece by piece. Players expecting action-heavy horror or constant encounters may find the deliberate pacing too slow, but those who appreciate exploration-driven experiences are more likely to enjoy the game's design philosophy.

Wooden Floor 2: Resurrection succeeds by focusing on suspense, environmental storytelling, and player-driven discovery rather than relying on nonstop scares. Its branching endings, expanded exploration, and stronger narrative ambitions make it a worthwhile improvement over the original, while its haunting atmosphere remains its most memorable achievement. Although some rough mechanics and occasional pacing issues prevent it from reaching the level of more polished horror titles, it stands as a respectable indie effort that demonstrates creativity and passion throughout its relatively concise adventure. Fans of psychological horror, mystery, and exploration-based gameplay will likely find plenty to appreciate beneath its rough edges.

Rating: 5/10
